prerequisites: Knowledge of the basics of materials science
Knowledge of conventional processing technologies and components

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the most suitable welding techniques for the permanent joining of mechanical elements.
Define non-destructive tests suitable for the qualification of a mechanical component or structure.
Define systems based on artificial intelligence for process monitoring.
Identify the most suitable robotic systems to be used to integrate the different technologies, develop the processing programs.
Evaluate the environmental impact and sustainability of the processes covered by the course.
Be able to identify the most appropriate machining and inspection strategies to create or verify components that meet the specifications imposed by the drawing.
Know how to identify suitable systems for the automation of machining processes through robotics and the best approach to the programming of processes.
Know how to choose an AI-based system for process monitoring.
Be able to describe, in written form, in a clear and concise way and orally expose with language properties the objectives, the procedure and the results of the elaborations carried out.
To be able to apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those presented during the course, and to deepen the topics covered using materials other than those proposed.
The application of systems based on artificial intelligence.

syllabus_topics: General fusion welding (flame, electric arc, plasma, laser, pressure and resistance)
Solid state welding (friction, ultrasonic, electromagnetic pulse)
Thermomechanical and microstructural aspects of welded joints
Structure and operation of a robot
Axes and hints on direct and inverse kinematics
Introduction to Machine Learning and Deep Learning
Artificial intelligence systems and their applications to technologies
assessment_rules: The overall evaluation is expressed in thirtieths. The minimum evaluation level (18/30) is awarded when the student demonstrates a reduced understanding of the topics, poor expository ability, and limited autonomy and judgment skills. The maximum level (30/30) is awarded when the student demonstrates complete and in-depth knowledge, ability to solve problems, and remarkable ability in defining procedures. Honours are awarded for significant mastery of theoretical and operational contents, considerable language propriety, and autonomous processing skills.
